findings.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — userPermDenialCacheKey is keyed per (namespace,user,action,name,parentFolder) instead of per-action like the old permCache, so a caller who can vary `name`/`parentFolder` on CheckRequest (e.g. probing many non-existent resource names) can generate unbounded distinct cache entries per user/action, increasing cache cardinality/memory pressure versus the coarser prior design.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:126 — permDenialCache keys on (namespace,userUID,action,name,parentFolder), turning what was one coarse per-(namespace,userUID,action) cache entry into one entry per distinct resource denied, and the underlying cache.NewLocalCache(Config{Expiry,CleanupInterval}) has no entry-count cap, only TTL expiry, so memory scales with distinct denied (user,action,resource) combinations until the 30s shortCacheTTL/10min cleanup runs

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — getCachedIdentityPermissions treats a real error from GetUserIdentifiers (e.g. DB failure) the same as a cache miss, causing Check to redundantly retry the identical DB-backed lookup via getIdentityPermissions instead of failing fast

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:180 — List has the same fall-through-on-any-error pattern as Check: a genuine DB error from getCachedIdentityPermissions is masked as a cache miss and silently retried via getIdentityPermissions, doubling load on a failing dependency

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey/userPermCacheKey concatenate namespace, userUID, action, name, parent with plain "_" separators (no escaping), so distinct (userUID,action,name,parent) tuples can produce identical cache keys and a denial cached for one resource could be returned for a different resource (fail-closed mis-deny); exploitability is limited since K8s-style resource names/UIDs generally disallow "_"

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:973 — The "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" subtest pre-seeds permDenialCache via s.permDenialCache.Set directly instead of exercising Check()'s own `if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }` write path (service.go ~line 153), so that write is never covered by any test

goldens.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — userPermDenialCacheKey is keyed per (namespace,user,action,name,parentFolder) instead of per-action like the old permCache, so a caller who can vary `name`/`parentFolder` on CheckRequest (e.g. probing many non-existent resource names) can generate unbounded distinct cache entries per user/action, increasing cache cardinality/memory pressure versus the coarser prior design.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `permDenialCache` and keys it with `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace,userUID,action,name,parent)` (service.go: `permDenialKey := userPermDenialCacheKey(...)`), and stores a denial entry on any DB-evaluated deny (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true) }`). Because `name` and `parentFolder` come from the `CheckRequest`, callers can vary them to create many distinct cache keys for the same (namespace,user,action), increasing cache cardinality compared to the existing `permCache` which is keyed per (namespace,user,action). This is a concrete, diff-grounded resource/memory pressure concern, but not a directly verifiable correctness break from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:126 — permDenialCache keys on (namespace,userUID,action,name,parentFolder), turning what was one coarse per-(namespace,userUID,action) cache entry into one entry per distinct resource denied, and the underlying cache.NewLocalCache(Config{Expiry,CleanupInterval}) has no entry-count cap, only TTL expiry, so memory scales with distinct denied (user,action,resource) combinations until the 30s shortCacheTTL/10min cleanup runs

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new `permDenialCache` keyed by `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` (added in `cache.go` and used in `Service.Check`), which creates one cache entry per denied (user,action,resource,name,parentFolder) combination rather than the coarser per-(namespace,userUID,action) permission cache. The cache implementation shown in tests (`cache.NewLocalCache(cache.Config{Expiry, CleanupInterval})`) exposes only TTL-based eviction (no size/entry cap visible in this diff), so the number of denial entries can grow with distinct denied resources until expiry/cleanup. This is a performance/memory-scaling concern created by the change, not a directly verifiable correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — getCachedIdentityPermissions treats a real error from GetUserIdentifiers (e.g. DB failure) the same as a cache miss, causing Check to redundantly retry the identical DB-backed lookup via getIdentityPermissions instead of failing fast

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the result of `getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)` is only used when `err == nil`; any non-nil error (including a real error from `GetUserIdentifiers` inside `getCachedIdentityPermissions`) is ignored and the code falls through to `getIdentityPermissions(...)` (DB-backed) without returning/logging the original error. Since `getCachedIdentityPermissions` explicitly returns `err` from `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)`, this can cause an immediate redundant retry of the same identifier/permission lookup path rather than failing fast on a non-cache error. This is grounded in the new control flow added around the cached-permissions block in `Check` and the new `getCachedIdentityPermissions` implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:180 — List has the same fall-through-on-any-error pattern as Check: a genuine DB error from getCachedIdentityPermissions is masked as a cache miss and silently retried via getIdentityPermissions, doubling load on a failing dependency

adjudication.rationale: In List (service.go), the code treats any error from getCachedIdentityPermissions as a cache miss: `permissions, err := s.getCachedIdentityPermissions(...); if err == nil { ... } else { ... permissions, err = s.getIdentityPermissions(...) }`. getCachedIdentityPermissions can return non-cache-miss errors (e.g., it calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)` and returns that error directly), but List neither distinguishes `cache.ErrNotFound` nor logs/returns the original error. This can cause an extra call path to the underlying store/DB on real errors (and obscures the original failure), matching the finding’s “fall-through-on-any-error” concern. It’s primarily a resiliency/observability/perf issue rather than a clear functional correctness defect visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:973 — The "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" subtest pre-seeds permDenialCache via s.permDenialCache.Set directly instead of exercising Check()'s own `if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }` write path (service.go ~line 153), so that write is never covered by any test

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TestService_CacheCheck` subtest "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry", the denial is simulated by directly calling `s.permDenialCache.Set(...)` rather than triggering the new write path in `Service.Check` (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true) }` added in `service.go`). The diff shows no added test that asserts `Check()` itself populates `permDenialCache` after a computed denial, so the newly introduced caching-on-deny behavior is not exercised by these new tests.
